questions.question: Why must directions start from a clear starting point and direction?
questions.expected_answer: Because left and right change when you turn around. If the starting point and the direction you face are clear, then left and right will mean the same thing to the person following the directions.

questions.question: How do landmarks and road names make directions clearer? Give an example.
questions.expected_answer: They tell the person exactly where to turn and help them check they are on the right road. For example: at the water tower, turn right into Station Road.

questions.question: Write directions with at least one left turn, one right turn and one landmark.
questions.expected_answer: Any clear set of directions, for example: Stand at the school gate facing the road. Turn left and go straight on past the church. At the petrol station, turn right. The shop is on your left, next to the clinic.
